title: "Tools: adding clips"
description: The agent tools that place media, titles, shapes, adjustment clips and backgrounds on the timeline, with every argument, answer and refusal.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools put new clips on the timeline. Three place a media file, three make a clip with no source, and two make a backdrop on a new track of its own.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['add_clip', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip', 'add_adjustment_clip', 'add_background', 'add_blurred_background']}
/>

## What the tools share

Each one is one undo step. It answers `ok: true`, `new_clips` (the ids it made), `new_tracks` when it made a track, and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

Times and lengths are ticks, 600,000 per second, rounded to the project's frame grid. A negative `at` is taken as 0. Colours are four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

**`project`** is the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.

**`scope`** is a nest id. With it, the call's ids and times are looked up inside that nest. Without it, the call goes wherever the app is looking. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

**The overlap rule** stops a placement that breaks it. A clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half of the shorter clip, because an overlap is a transition. A new clip that overlaps the clip before it and has no transition gets a cross dissolve.

**A locked track** doesn't stop these tools, apart from `insert_clip`. Locks hold back gestures in the window and what a timeline-wide shift may touch.

## `add_clip`

Places a whole media file as one clip, as [dragging a Media-tab row onto a track](/editing/add-clips/#drag-media-onto-a-track) does.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. `get_project` lists them. |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. `import_media` returns one. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the clip starts on the timeline, in ticks. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to place it in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

The clip starts at source time 0 and runs the media's whole length, rounded down to whole frames so it never outruns the file. Trim it afterwards with [`trim_start`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start) and [`trim_end`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_end). A picture with no length of its own runs 5 seconds.

It's given Fit scale when the project's `fit_new_clips` is on, which it is by default, and the source is bigger than the canvas.

It's refused when it would break the overlap rule. A media shorter than a frame or with no duration can't be placed, and neither can a LUT, which is applied as a [look](/mcp/tools-set-video/). The step is called "Add Clip".

## `insert_clip`

The insert edit, as [**Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#insert-a-file) or <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dropping a Media-tab row does. It makes room for the whole media at `at`, so nothing is covered.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | Where to insert, in ticks. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to insert in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

In one step:

1. The clip `at` falls inside on `track` is split.
2. Every unlocked track opens by the media's length. Clips starting at or after `at` move later, and so do markers at or after it.
3. The media lands in the hole.

Only the destination track is cut. A clip straddling `at` on another track stays whole, which is what keeps a music bed unbroken. The exception is a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at `at` too and paired with it.

It's refused when `track` is locked, because the room can't be made there, and when a step of the edit is refused, in that step's own words. A media `add_clip` can't place can't be inserted either. The step is called "Insert".

## `overwrite_clip`

The overwrite edit, as [**Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#overwrite-with-a-file) or <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd>-dropping a Media-tab row does. It takes the room instead of making it.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | Where to overwrite, in ticks. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to overwrite in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

The span the media needs is cleared on `track` alone: cut at both ends, and whatever is left inside removed. Nothing shifts, so the cut's length and every other track stay as they are.

The exception is a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at the same bounds and paired. The partner's middle piece stays, unlinked.

The named track is cleared even when it's locked. It's refused when the clip can't be placed once the span is clear, and a media `add_clip` can't place can't be used here either. The step is called "Overwrite".

## `add_text_clip`

Adds a text clip, a title, as the [**Add Text**](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#add-a-text-clip) button does. It has no source, so it can be any length. Style it afterwards with `set_text` and place it with `set_video`.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
| `text` | object or string | No | A plain string is the words. An object is a `set_text` patch merged over the Title preset. Default: the preset's own placeholder, "Title". |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

A new clip is the Title preset: 72 px white Source Sans 3 Bold, centred. An object can set anything [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) can, including `content`, `font`, `size`, `color`, `align`, `valign`, `outline`, `backdrop`, `width`, `animation`, `case`, `words` and `word_style`. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).

```json
{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "text": "Chapter one" }
{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "duration": 1200000,
  "text": { "content": "Chapter one", "size": 96, "align": "left" } }
```

It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown key or a bad value in the patch, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Add Text".

## `add_shape_clip`

Adds a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow drawn over the video, as [**Add Shape**](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip) does. Like text, it has no source and can be any length. [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) changes it afterwards and `set_video` places it.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
| `shape` | object or string | No | A plain string is a kind: `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line` or `arrow`. An object is a `set_shape` patch merged over the default rectangle. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

Leave out `shape` for the default: a 320×120 rectangle, outlined with no fill. An object can set `kind`, `width`, `height`, `stroke`, `fill`, `radius`, `arrow_start`, `arrow_end`, `from`, `to` and `gradient`.

A rounded rectangle is a rectangle with a `radius`, not a kind of its own. An arrow is created with its head on, so pass `arrow_end: false` for a bare diagonal. A box bigger than the canvas gets Fit scale when `fit_new_clips` is on, as oversized footage does.

It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown kind, key or value, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Add Shape".

## `add_adjustment_clip`

Adds an adjustment clip, as [**Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) does. It has no picture of its own. While it lasts, it grades everything drawn behind it: every lower track and the canvas background, never a track in front.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

Grade it with [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/): `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, `qualifier`, and the point filters (sepia, noir, vignette and invert). Its `opacity` is the grade's strength. On a track cut by a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) it grades only inside the matte, and on a matte track it does nothing.

It's refused:

- inside a nest, whether you pass `scope` or a nest is open
- in any transition or overlap. Fade it with `opacity` instead.

Later, `set_video` gives an error for blur, sharpen, pixelate or a blend mode on it. The step is called "Add Adjustment Clip".

## `add_background`

Puts a backdrop on a new back-most track, starting at 0 and running the timeline's length, as [**Clip ▸ Add Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/) does. The clip is named "Background".

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | array of four numbers | No | The plate's colour, as `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. White when left out. |
| `media` | integer | No | A media id to show instead of a colour. `import_media` adds a file. |
| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default: the whole timeline's length, and never less than one frame. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

With no arguments it's a canvas-sized white rectangle, which is what the menu's **Solid Color** row sends. It's white because the canvas is already black, so a black plate would appear to do nothing. A full-canvas gradient is this clip with [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/)'s `gradient` after it.

With `media` the picture goes there at Fill scale, where `add_clip` would Fit it, because a plate that leaves the canvas showing down one side has failed. A video plate stops where its file does, whatever `duration` says. A picture runs the timeline, or for `duration` when you give one.

It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.

These are errors, and nothing is added:

- `media` and `color` together
- a `duration` under one frame
- a media with no pictures, such as a sound file
- a colour that isn't four numbers from 0 to 1

The step is called "Add Background".

## `add_blurred_background`

The screencast backdrop, as [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) does. It copies a clip onto a new back-most track at the same start, duration, speed and source window, so the two play exactly the same frames.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. `get_project` lists them. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

The copy is named "Blurred Background". It's scaled to fill the canvas, centred, uncropped, blended normally and blurred at full strength.

Its sound is off, or the mix would play one recording twice. It drops the original's ducking, because a copy keeping it would duck the whole mix, and it drops its transition, actions and label too.

It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.

These are errors, and nothing is added:

- a nest clip, whose copy would come out sharp
- a source with no pixel size, such as a text clip or a sound-only clip
- a clip with no video properties

The step is called "Add Blurred Background".
---
title: "Tools: moving and trimming"
description: The agent tools that move clips, trim their edges, slip their source, roll a cut and switch a clip's picture or sound, with every argument and refusal.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools change where a clip sits and what it shows. They name clips by id, so read them from `get_project` first.

<AtAGlance tools={['move_clip', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'slip', 'roll', 'set_enabled']} />

## What the tools share

Each one is one undo step. It answers `ok: true` and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

**Clamped, not refused.** Most of these hold a time to what the clip's source allows and do as much as they can. Read the clip back to see where it landed. When the limits leave nothing to do, the answer says "*Step* made no change", and no undo step is made.

**Times** are ticks, 600,000 per second, rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

**`project`** is the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.

**`scope`** is a nest id. With it, the call's ids and times are looked up inside that nest. Without it, the call goes wherever the app is looking. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

**Linked pairs.** After [`detach_audio`](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/), a picture and its sound move together. The partner comes along only when it's on an unlocked track. A lock on a named clip's own track doesn't stop these tools.

**A boolean** may also be sent as `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`.

## `move_clip`

Shifts clips along the timeline, and optionally onto another track, as [dragging a clip](/editing/move-clips/) does.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
| `delta` | integer | Yes | How far to shift, in ticks. Negative moves earlier. |
| `track` | integer | No | The destination track for the first clip. The first clip is the one on the back-most track, then the earliest. Leave it out to stay on the current tracks. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clips are in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

Several clips keep their relative track offsets, so a selection spanning two tracks lands two tracks apart.

Starts stop at 0. It's the earliest clip that stops there, linked partners included, and the rest keep their distance from it.

A linked pair moves together in time, but only the clips you name change track. So you can drop a sound half onto a track of its own while its picture stays.

It's refused:

- when the destination breaks the overlap rule: a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half of the shorter clip
- when a clip would land off either end of the track list

A clip that gains an overlap with the clip before it, and has no transition, gains a `cross_dissolve`. The step is called "Move Clip".

## `trim_start`

Moves a clip's start, as [dragging its left edge](/editing/trimming/) or pressing <kbd>W</kbd> does. The content stays in place: the source's in point advances by the same amount, so nothing after the new start shifts.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
| `to` | integer | Yes | The new start, in ticks. |
| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this clip's edge without its linked partner's, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). The timeline does this for a dragged sound. Default `false`. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

It stops at the source's own beginning and one frame short of the clip's end, because a clip is at least one frame long.

On a linked pair, the other half's start follows when it was the same as this clip's.

Timed words stay on the speech they time, and a graphic's own clock moves with the edge. Actions stay where they are in the clip. See [What a trim keeps](/editing/trimming/#what-a-trim-keeps).

On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after the new start can change. The start is held where the clip still fits its media.

It's refused when the new start would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Trim Start".

## `trim_end`

Moves a clip's end, as [dragging its right edge](/editing/trimming/) or pressing <kbd>E</kbd> does.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

---
title: "Close gaps and insert time"
description: "Close an empty stretch of a track with a double-click or Close Gap, and open room on the timeline when you need it."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Closing a gap pulls everything after it back to meet what's before it, on every unlocked track, so the timeline stays in sync. Opening room does the opposite.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Close Gap"
  where="Double-click an empty stretch of a lane"
  tools={['close_gap', 'insert_time']}
/>

## Double-click a gap

Double-click an empty stretch of a lane. Everything after the gap, on every unlocked track, moves left by the gap's length. It's one undo step, named Close Gap.

This only works on a lane. Above the first lane or below the last, no track is named, so there's nothing to close.

## Close the gap under the playhead

Move the playhead into a gap and choose **Clip ▸ Close Gap**. It has no shortcut.

It works on the current track: the selected clip's track or, with nothing selected, the front track. The result is the same as a double-click. The command is available when the timeline has clips.

## What moves

- A gap is the empty stretch between two clips on that track. A gap before the first clip closes back to the start of the timeline.
- Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after the far side of the gap moves left. A clip on another track that spans that point stays where it is.
- A moved clip's [linked partner](/audio/detach-and-attach/) moves too, when its track is unlocked.
- [Markers](/timeline/markers/) don't move.
- A clip that ends up overlapping the one before it, within the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), gets a Cross Dissolve.

## When a gap won't close

A gap closes completely or not at all. Frame Job beeps, moves nothing and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector when:

| What's wrong | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The point is on a clip, not in a gap | Move the playhead into the gap, or check the current track. |
| No clip follows the gap on that track | There's nothing to pull back. |
| The track is locked | [Unlock it](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). Its clips are the ones that would stay behind. |
| Closing it would push clips into an overlap the overlap rule forbids, on any track that moves | Trim or move those clips first. |
| A linked clip would go before the start of the timeline | Happens when a sound leads its picture, as in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). Trim the front of the sound so it leads by less. |

## Insert time

Inserting time opens empty room. Every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later by a length, and so does every marker at or after that point, unlike a ripple.

Clips that span the point stay put, so nothing is cut. To open room inside a clip, [split](/editing/splitting/) it first.

Inserting time has no menu item or gesture of its own. An ⌥-drop [insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) and [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) both do it as part of their edit, and an agent can do it directly with `insert_time`. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

## Open room by hand

title: Freeze frame
description: Hold the frame under the playhead for 2 seconds, keep the rest of the cut in sync, and choose which frame the still holds.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Freeze Frame holds one moment of a clip on screen for 2 s, then lets the clip carry on. Use it to pause on a reaction, or to give a title or a voice-over time to land.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Freeze Frame"
  keys="⇧⌘F"
  tools={['freeze_frame', 'slip']}
/>

## Freeze a frame

<Steps>

1. Select the clip.

2. Move the playhead to the frame you want to hold.

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame**, or press <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>.

</Steps>

Frame Job splits the clip at the playhead, opens 2 s of empty time there, and fills the gap on the clip's track with a still of that source frame. The rest of the clip picks up after the still. All of this is one undo step, called **Freeze Frame**.

The still has no sound, so the clip's own sound stops for the hold.

If the playhead sits on the clip's first frame, there's nothing to cut. The still goes in and the whole clip moves after it.

## When it is available

Freeze Frame works on a selected clip under the playhead. With nothing selected there, it's dimmed. A playhead exactly at a clip's end isn't on that clip. With several selected clips under the playhead, it acts on the first.

It needs a clip of a video file with its picture. An audio-only clip, text, a shape, a picture, a graphic, an adjustment clip, a nest or another still can't be frozen. The command stays available on those, and Frame Job shows an error saying the clip isn't a media clip or has no video properties. Nothing changes.

## Everything stays in sync

The 2 s opens across every unlocked track, so the cut stays together:

- Clips that start at or after the playhead move 2 s later, on every unlocked track.
- Markers at or after the playhead move with them.
- A clip on another track that crosses the playhead is neither cut nor moved. It plays on through the hold, as a music bed would.
- Sound [linked](/audio/detach-and-attach/) to the frozen clip is cut at the playhead too, and its second half moves with the picture.
- Clips on locked tracks stay where they are.

title: "Type a clip's timing"
description: "Trim a clip to an exact time by typing its In and Out, and read its length, in the Clip tab's Timing section."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Timing section is for when you know the number. Type where a clip starts and ends on the timeline, and read how long it is, without dragging an edge.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing"
  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
/>

## Type In and Out

<Steps>

1. Select one clip.

2. In the [inspector's](/getting-started/inspector/) **Clip** tab, choose the **Clip** sub-tab, the last one. **Timing** is its first section. When the section is shut, its header still shows the clip's length, so click the header to open it.

3. Click **In** or **Out** and type a time. `1:23`, `83.5` and `1:23:04` all work, as they do in the toolbar's time field. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).

4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>.

</Steps>

| Field | What it is | What typing does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | Where the clip starts on the timeline | Trims its front edge. The rest of the clip stays where it is. |
| **Out** | Where the clip ends on the timeline | Trims its back edge. |

Both are positions on the timeline, not positions in the file. A later **In** hides the start of the footage, and an earlier one brings it back. To move the whole clip without trimming it, [drag it](/editing/move-clips/) instead.

Each change is one undo step, named Trim Start or Trim End. The time lands on the project's frame grid.

## How far an edge can go

A number out of range doesn't beep. The edge goes as far as it can, and the field shows where it landed.

| Field | Earliest | Latest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | The start of the timeline, or as far back as the file has footage | One frame before the clip's end |
| **Out** | One frame after the clip's start | As far as the file has footage |

Only a clip that plays a video or audio file has a footage limit. Text, shapes, pictures and graphics have no file length to run out of.

content.content:
A graphic is drawn fresh at a size you choose, and it has an animation timeline of its own. The **Size** and **Timeline** sections of the **Graphic** sub-tab set both, so you can make a graphic sharp at any size and decide whether its outro follows the end of the clip.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Size', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Timeline']}
  tools={['set_graphic', 'set_video', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}

**Fit to Canvas** in the **Size** section sets the size to the canvas's, then centres the clip at scale 1. It works on every selected graphic clip, as one undo step called Fit Graphic to Canvas.

A graphic can't be larger than 8192 pixels a side, so on a bigger canvas Frame Job tells you why and leaves the clip as it was.

## The graphic's own timeline

A graphic counts its own frames from its first frame, separately from the project's timeline. The **Timeline** section shows where the clip sits on that count. It appears only when one clip is selected, it starts collapsed, and its header shows the length.

22:- A slip stops when the clip reaches either end of its file, and keeps what it reached. It doesn't turn into a trim. If there's no footage to slide into, the drag changes nothing.
25:- A [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) slips too, which changes the frame it holds. It stops one frame short of the end of its file.
43:- A clip that plays a file can't grow past what the file has. Text, shapes and pictures have no such limit.
70:- On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the actions stay where they are and the limits come from the ramp, so a cut stops rolling where the clip would no longer fit its file.
